(Photo by Dustin Satloff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just when I thought we were hunting for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NBA Draft… …Mike Brown and the lads decided to get their excrement together and remind us the Knicks are actually a title contender. Here’s the latest before we turn the page quickly to this evening’s affair against the Chicago Oxen. "Close to 48 minutes of basketball we know how to play and we like to play" Mike Brown's opening statement after tonight's win vs. the Pistons pic.twitter.com/37x3ivgfnl — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 28, 2026 Mike Brown On facing the Pistons despite Detroit dominating the Knicks last season: “We have to concentrate on the next opponent in front of us, and Detroit happens to be that opponent. And, they had our number last year, you know. It is what it is, that’s kind of how the NBA is [and] it works. I said this before, one of the years we won it when I was in Golden State as an assistant. We lost the season series to Utah, I don’t know, it was 0-4, 1-3. One game, we got I think, beat by 40. “So, you know, I don’t necessarily take a ton of [stock in it]. Obviously, you want to win, you want to be in good position for a playoff run, but I don’t take a ton of stock in, they won this series or they killed us in this [regular season] series because playoff season is a different ballgame.” On experimenting with Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns’ minutes and rotations during the first games of the season: “No, no, no, no. You can always get better. You guys probably don’t notice, you probably never picked up on it but in Games 1 and 2 [of this season], my big experimentation was playing [Karl-Anthony Towns] and Jalen in two stretches together. And so the middle of it, I had both KAT and Jalen off the floor. We didn’t really do that last year. “Watching it, I didn’t like it. So last game was the first game that I went back to [keeping one on the floor]. So there’s some things that I’m looking at or messing with that may or may not stay the same. “That’s part of what you’re trying to do to figure out what’s best for your team long term. In the short term, it might not turn out good, like it didn’t turn out good not starting Josh, we took our lumps. But it was good to go through it last year. So, it’s something we’ll continue to try to figure out early on.” On challenging Karl-Anthony Towns at halftime against the Pistons and his 27-20 outing: “I challenged KAT and KAT had a tremendous second half. Twenty-seven and 20, he’s more than capable of doing that night in and night out. “KAT’s a grown man. He’s obviously a perennial All-Star. I just told him the truth: ‘KAT, the guy is killing us on the glass, and when he gets a rebound, he’s putting it back. Anything he gets in the paint, he’s putting it back. If he catches on the perimeter, guard him,’” “And he did those things. I’ve got to take my hat off to KAT because I thought his shift in his mindset was really big for us in the second half.” On the Knicks dictating the physicality against Detroit: “Once our guys realized, ‘No, no, I can’t react to them, I gotta dictate to them what’s gonna happen,’ and they do it with a smart level of physicality, then it makes it easier [to defend].” On the Knicks putting together a more complete performance in their first win: “We talk about trying to string a game together. 48 minutes of basketball the way we know how to play, and we like to play. And we had some lulls where we weren’t as physical as we should have been throughout the course of the game, but we had some really good moments. We had more good moments in this game in totality than we did in the first three games, and that’s why we got the win.” On the Knicks’ early struggles being part of the process of preparing for the playoffs: “We can have some hiccups. That’s what the [regular] season’s for. It’s trying to correct it, so come playoff time, you’re ready to go do what you need to do. So is it fixed? No, it ain’t fixed. Nothing’s really fixed. “What tonight shows us is we’re more than capable if we put our minds to it. And that’s what we gotta continue to try to build off. And then if we do slip up, that we don’t slip up for eight minutes or 10 minutes. Maybe for a minute and a half, two minutes, and then we get back, regroup, and get back heading in the right direction again.” On the Knicks’ shot selection and overall performance against Detroit: “I still believe we took some really good shots. I believe if we keep taking the shots that we’re taking, they’re going to start going in sooner than later. But our guys played an overall good game. On the offensive glass, defensively physically, offensively physically.” On the Knicks doing a better job defending Detroit’s designated shooters: “The guys that we labeled hot tonight, two of the guys were obviously Duncan Robinson and [Daniss] Jenkins, and they were combined 3-for-16. So our awareness, our level of physicality, throughout the 48 minutes were a lot better on those two guys in the previous game.” On the Knicks’ performance against Detroit compared with their first three losses: “I give our guys credit. We talked about trying to string a game together, close to 48 minutes, the way we can play and like to play. We had some lulls where we weren’t as physical as we should have been. But we had some good moments. We had more good moments in totality than the first three games.” On lessons from the Warriors’ 2018 championship defense and avoiding panic: “The one thing that I do know [about that season] is nobody ever panicked, from the ownership to the [general manager] to coaching staff all down through players. We just truly felt we were better than the way we were playing. “At that point in the season, to go through getting thumped in the head sometimes, might not be all bad, you know? So I think that’s the biggest thing is to know that you’ve got a game plan and you want to stay the course. Make some tweaks here, make some tweaks there.” Jalen Brunson was asked what he thinks drives Josh Hart's mentality: "Popcorn, candy, wine and caffeine. He's a different person" 😭 pic.twitter.com/GubelpZNTA — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 28, 2026 Jalen Brunson On a challenging start to the season: “Everyone can say it’s obviously early in the season. We could use that as an excuse. But I think the one thing that I see is when we get those runs, when we start to look like the team that we’ve been in the past, we get a little comfortable. So we’ve got to continue to put our foot on the gas and execute things that we did last year. “And we’re not going to be the same. We’re not going to be the way we were playing last year. That’s just human nature. But we have to accept this part of the journey, find a way to be better. And hopefully, throughout a couple of games, we’re going to look back on it and say, ‘Yeah, we grew from that.’” On responding to early-season adversity and the sky-high expectations of a title defense: “Find whatever it takes to win. Control what we can control. Focus on the little details that might seem small but can impact winning. Most importantly, stick together. One thing I’ve said during training camp and to this day is we’re going to see who we are within the first couple weeks of the season. And we’re seeing adversity so how are we going to respond? “We’re going to get everyone’s best because of last year. Everyone has been telling us what a great job we did, how fun it was, what we did for the city, the constant praise and so we need to be the opposite.” O n the Knicks’ identity after earning their first win: “We’re the Knicks, actually.” On the Knicks’ defensive turnaround against Detroit: “We talked about it and we knew we needed to do it. I think the way we played that second quarter really turned things around and helped us take control of the game.” On the Knicks’ need for patience: “We got to remember that Rome wasn’t built in a day. This is a new year, new team. Adversity started early, so we just gotta fight back. We have a long way to go, but obviously we want to learn from wins as much as we do from losses. Excited we came up with the win today.” On Karl-Anthony Towns stepping up against Paul Reed and the Pistons on Tuesday: “[Reed] played great in the first half. I think we were able to not let him loose on the offensive boards. He was really impacting the game. For [KAT] to step up as he did throughout the game was something that we needed.” On Josh Hart’s sources of energy: “Popcorn, candy, wine and caffeine. He’s just a different person.” Karl-Anthony Towns on what changed for the Knicks coming out of halftime tonight "I thought we did a better job picking up on our intensity and our physicality and we executed at a high level. We've got to worry about the controllables, which is playing our best" pic.twitter.com/wPdkAzct2U — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 28, 2026 Karl-Anthony Towns On staying optimistic despite the Knicks’ 0-3 start: “As much as you lose nine out of 11, it’s the way you can win 13 straight. So just stay faithful, stay faithful, continue to put the work in, continue to find different ways we could be better. We’ve just gotta get back to the drawing board. Back to what made us so special last year. We have to tap back into that kind of mojo, that magic, and find ways to do what we got to do to get it back up.” On the Knicks resembling last season’s championship team against Detroit: “More like ourselves from last year.” On the Knicks increasing their physicality and intensity against the Pistons: “I thought we did a better job picking up our intensity and our physicality, and we just executed at a high level. We’ve just got to worry about the controllables, which is us playing our best, executing at a high level, and bringing that physicality to the game.” On the Knicks executing the fundamentals against Detroit: “We did all the little things tonight. That’s how we got the W.” On the need for building momentum after the first win: “Gotta get the next one. Build off of this game and continue to improve as a team. All year it’s gonna be us improving, going through the ups and downs of a season. We just gotta stay steady, keep believing in each other, keep pushing each other to another level.” On wanting to reward Knicks fans after three disappointing losses: “It’s been an ongoing thing. These fans deserve the best of us and we haven’t given them that the first three games. We wanted to give them something to cheer for.” Josh Hart so unserious lmaooo. Scuffle going on and he fake squared up on Pistons assistant coach Jarrett Jack and SCARED the sh*t out of him 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/D75g5uwcxR — Hater Report (@HaterReport) October 28, 2026

stories.title: AJ Dybantsa to make season debut for Washington Wednesday night in Cleveland
stories.summary: The Wizards' No. 1 pick will make his debut after sitting out the first four games with an ankle sprain.
stories.detailText: AJ Dybantsa, the No. 1 pick last June, will officially make his NBA debut Wednesday night in Cleveland. No more waiting ⌛️ @AJ_Dybantsa pic.twitter.com/XCZ65MiPho — Washington Wizards (@WashWizards) October 28, 2026 Dybantsa, 19, missed the Wizards' first four games this season due to a sprained left ankle suffered late in training camp. He steps into a Wizards offense already loaded with firepower, including Trae Young and Anthony Davis, the latter of whom has had a couple of very impressive games to start the season. Dybantsa comes to Washington as the hope for the future, the top pick who will change the fortunes of a long-middling (or worse) franchise. Dybantsa was a standout at BYU, averaging 25.5 points a game, and followed that with an impressive Summer League. Dybantsa looked like a rookie still finding his footing in the preseason, averaging 12.8 points per game, shooting just 18.2% from 3-point range. But that's just the preseason. Starting Wednesday night, things get real.

stories.title: The Suns’ small-ball problem starts with a problem they can’t control
stories.summary: Phoenix is missing its two primary centers, making small ball a necessity rather than a preferred strategy.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 24: Yaxel Lendeborg #1 of the Golden State Warriors attempts a layup against Luke Kennard #8 and Ryan Dunn #0 of the Phoenix Suns during the second half at Mortgage Matchup Center on October 24, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. The Suns defeated the Warriors 131-122. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Small-ball lineups have been the bane of Jordan Ott’s existence during his early tenure with the Phoenix Suns, as through his first season and three games, it appears that they simply don’t work. The team compromises on rebounding to prioritize athleticism and flexibility. In theory, you should be able to play five out and shoot the ball effectively, but the Suns aren’t particularly good at shooting the ball. But here’s where two harsh realities need to take root, at least based on the small sample size we’ve experienced through the first three games. First off, you don’t have to look exclusively at small-ball lineups to recognize the undeniable truth that the starting five hasn’t played particularly well together either. The combination of Booker, Brooks, Bridges, Green, and Khaman Maluach has logged 37 minutes together, producing a net rating of -35.5 and an offensive rating of 94.7. The second is that small-ball lineups exist within the Phoenix Suns’ ecosystem out of necessity rather than by schematic preference. Ott isn’t sending Miles Bridges out there at the five because he thinks it’s a strategic advantage. Mark Williams is injured. Oso Ighodaro is injured. That’s a seven-footer and a 6’10” big man who are simply unavailable. The Suns are rolling out small ball lineups because they have to. And yes, some of those lineups have been absolutely blasted early on. To the moon. Take the combination of Collin Gillespie, Jalen Green, Devin Booker, Dillon Brooks, and Miles Bridges. That group has played a total of 6 minutes across 2 games and has a net rating of -105.2. I didn’t know that was possible. It is. What’s interesting, however, is that the five-man lineup with the second-most minutes played this season features Collin Gillespie, Jordan Goodwin, Luke Kennard, Miles Bridges, and Ryan Dunn. Would you call that one small? I sure would. Yet that group has an offensive rating of 131.8, a defensive rating of 100.0, and a net rating of +31.8. Gasp! So all this pounding the table about the small-ball lineups Ott is putting on the floor is based on a false premise. He’s not doing it by design, and within that context, one of the combinations he’s deployed has actually been productive. If your response is, “Well, they should throw Rasheer Fleming into the fold because he has size,” let’s remember a few things. First, he’s still only 6’9”… so he would be too small as compared to the opposing center’s size. Second, think back to the preseason and the challenges he experienced in understanding his spacing and where he needed to be on the floor. Now ask him to know where to be as a five. Good luck with that. Third, when Fleming has played as the small-ball five alongside Gillespie, Goodwin, Bridges, and Dunn, that group has produced an offensive rating of 33.3 and a net rating of -36.7 over five minutes. That ‘disease of what if’ relative to Fleming isn’t a quality argument for his insertion into this shit show. There’s a lot wrong with this team right now, of that there is no doubt. And once again, we’re searching for the person responsible, the individual upon whom we can place the blame. For some people, that finger points directly at Jordan Ott. I’m not suggesting he’s without sin in this situation. I’m simply making the point that the small ball philosophy is being forced upon him rather than chosen, much like what we witnessed during the back end of last season. Even within those circumstances, there are some positives worth recognizing. The Suns have real problems to solve, and small ball hasn’t exactly covered itself in glory through the first three games. But context matters. Phoenix is playing without its two primary centers, the starting lineup hasn’t found its footing, and at least one smaller combination has produced encouraging results. Jordan Ott deserves scrutiny, but he also deserves a fair evaluation of the circumstances he’s navigating. Before we declare small ball a failed experiment, let’s see what happens when the Suns actually have the personnel to make other choices.

stories.title: Wizards' AJ Dybantsa set to make NBA debut Wednesday vs. Cavaliers
stories.summary: An ankle injury sidelined the 2026 No. 1 overall draft pick for four games.
stories.detailText: Washington Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa will make his long-awaited NBA regular-season debut Wednesday on the road against the Cleveland Cavaliers, the team announced . Dybantsa, the No. 1 pick in June's NBA Draft, did not play in Washington's first four games after suffering an ankle injury in the team's preseason finale on Oct. 16 . He was listed as questionable heading into the game against the Cavaliers, but was upgraded to available on Wednesday morning. During that preseason game against the New Orleans Pelicans, Dybantsa left the game early after landing awkwardly on his left ankle following a shot. He limped to the locker room for further evaluation and did not return. No more waiting ⌛️ @AJ_Dybantsa pic.twitter.com/XCZ65MiPho — Washington Wizards (@WashWizards) October 28, 2026 Before the injury, Dybantsa averaged 13 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2 steals in three preseason games. The Wizards have started the season 2-2, winning against the Milwaukee Bucks in their season opener as well as against the Chicago Bulls. They've dropped games against the Toronto Raptors and Charlotte Hornets. Barring injury, Dybantsa will make his home debut on Friday against the Hornets. Justin Champagnie undergoes foot surgery While the Wizards got good news on Dybantsa, there was bad news regarding forward Justin Champagnie. The Wizards announced on Wednesday that the 25-year-old underwent surgery to repair a fractured right foot and is out indefintely. He suffered the injury in the opening quarter of Monday's loss to Charlotte. Champagnie, who is in his sixth NBA season out of Pittsburgh, is averaging 7.3 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists through four games this season.

stories.title: NBA Injury Report: Who to add with Anthony Edwards, Tyrese Haliburton, Paolo Banchero and other stars sidelined
stories.summary: Dan Titus breaks down the fantasy impact of the NBA's early-season wave of injuries.
stories.detailText: It's been a week and a half of injury hell to start the NBA season, and the bodies keep dropping. What hurts more is the caliber of players falling victim to unfortunate circumstances. Anthony Edwards, Jalen Williams, Paolo Banchero, Kawhi Leonard, Jalen Duren, Jaren Jackson Jr., Cason Wallace, Jalen Suggs and Ivica Zubac are all out — with a handful of others who haven't played yet. Here's who's hurt, how long they might be gone and the viable fantasy replacements. Minnesota Timberwolves: Anthony Edwards Edwards is set to undergo arthroscopic surgery on his right knee and is expected to miss up to two months, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. That's a gut punch after a start that included two 40-plus-point games, including 47 in Monday's overtime loss at Cleveland. He had been playing through knee pain and fantasy managers will be disappointed to have to stash him on IR until at least January. In what looked like the start of an MVP-like campaign, Edwards won't be eligible for seasonal awards but hopefully will return during the second half of the season to help the Timberwolves (and fantasy managers) get a championship. The replacements: Ayo Dosunmu (75% rostered) is the obvious next man up to replace Edwards in the starting unit. He's averaging 12-4-4 in 26 minutes through four games. When Edwards missed time with a knee injury at the end of last season, Dosunmu stepped up, averaging 19-6-4 with 1 steal in 33 minutes across seven games. If he's gone, Terrence Shannon Jr. (20%) is the one to grab. He's averaging 13.0 points and 2.5 3s in 22 minutes. Jonathan Kuminga (64%) got his first double-double with the Wolves on Monday and should also see an expanded role in the rotation. Indiana Pacers: Tyrese Haliburton After missing the entire 2025-26 season recovering from a ruptured right Achilles, Haliburton’s return has hit another setback. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, Haliburton suffered a left hamstring strain and is without a timetable to return. He averaged 21.8 points and 9.5 assists through his first four games, but this latest injury raises concerns after such a lengthy absence. The Pacers will likely take a cautious approach with their franchise guard. The replacements : Andrew Nembhard will likely takeover point guard duties with other capable creators like Pascal Siakam adding to his workload. Beyond Nembhard, Quenton Jackson (1% rostered) is the next player I’d consider in deeper fantasy leagues, particularly if Haliburton misses extended time. Thunder: Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren Williams has a dislocated left ankle and a fractured fibula and will need surgery. No recovery timeline has been provided, but J-Dub is likely out for the rest of the season. For fantasy purposes, he's a drop in most leagues unless you have an IL spot that you're not using and want to wait for an update on the slim chances for a return late in the season. Wallace has a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will need surgery. He's expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. Holmgren is dealing with right knee patellar tendinitis, which has kept him out for one game thus far. By all accounts, Holmgren's injury seems more like a day-to-day issue. Still, fantasy managers need to keep tabs on it. The replacements: Ajay Mitchell (75%) is the biggest winner, averaging 16-3-4 with 2.5 stocks after a 30-point, 5-assist breakout on Monday. He's questionable Wednesday with an ankle sprain against Dallas, so check his status before lineups lock. Jared McCain (41%) started Monday and had 18 points with 4 3s and he'll be a reliable source of points and 3s going forward. Aday Mara (18%) is worth a look in deep leagues, with 11 points and 10 boards in 20 minutes Monday while filling in for Holmgren. Chet remains out on Wednesday, leaving the door open for another Mara stream. Orlando Magic: Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs Banchero has a low-grade high-ankle sprain that he suffered against the Timberwolves last week and is expected to miss 4-6 weeks. Jalen Suggs will miss at least the next two weeks after suffering a mild bone bruise in his right knee. The non-contact injury occurred late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over the New York Knicks. Suggs will be reevaluated in two weeks and fortunately, there was no structural damage. The replacements: Franz Wagner stands to benefit most, but from a waiver wire perspective, Tristan da Silva (22% rostered) will earn more minutes along with Anthony Black (68% rostered). Black is coming off a strong season debut, scoring 18 points with 5 3s and 5 assists. Da Silva is averaging 13-2-2 with 3 3s per game in 28 minutes. Jase Richardson (1%) is a deep league option, though; he's yet to surpass 20 minutes in any game. Toronto Raptors: Kawhi Leonard Leonard is expected to miss a period of weeks with swelling in his left knee, per Charania . An MRI revealed no structural damage and Toronto will re-evaluate him in a week. He's posted 19.5 points, 7.5 boards and 3.5 steals in his first two games. The thing about Kawhi is, we don't know what a period of weeks really means. Is this something that will be an in-and-out-of-the-lineup type of deal? Will the ramp-up and rehab management program be enough to alleviate sporadic load management days? This is part of the frustration with drafting Kawhi — you really don't know when his knee issues will flare up. The replacements: Ja'Kobe Walter (23%) started in his place Sunday and will be a decent source of points, 3s and steals. So far this season, Walter is averaging 13.0 points, 2.7 3s and 2.3 steals in 26 minutes per night. Rookie Allen Graves (3%) had 11 points, six boards and four assists Sunday and is a deep-league stash. Expect to see more RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles taking more shares on offense. Detroit Pistons: Jalen Duren Duren will be re-evaluated in two weeks, so he's looking at a return around Nov. 9. Duren was on my avoid list primarily because he missed a majority of the offseason in a contract dispute with Detroit's front office. The few times I watched Duren this summer, he looked like he stayed in shape and was actively working on his game. Fantasy managers took him confidently in the third rounds, but perhaps his conditioning wasn't quite where it should've been. To suffer a hamstring injury so early in the season isn't a good look for anyone. Time can heal, so let's be optimistic that we'll see him at full strength by early November. The replacements: Paul Reed (55%) is the add. He's up from 11% last Thursday, and he's averaging 11.0 points and 8.3 rebounds as the starting center. He had an impressive outing on Tuesday, coming through with 22-9-3 with 3 stocks in just 26 minutes. John Collins (83%) is likely rostered already. Utah Jazz: Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen Jackson has a torn MCL in his right knee and will miss 6-8 weeks according to Charania. He's out until at least mid-December, but the injury is nothing to play with. The timeline sounds good, but with rehab, minutes restrictions and a ramp-up period required, those steps may make the injury drag out longer than the initial timeline. It was a fluke injury, which makes this even more annoying. Markkanen left Monday's contest with a wrist injury and did not return. He's listed as day-to-day and is questionable for Wednesday, so fantasy managers will have to be patient. At least it wasn't anything too serious to keep him out longer. The replacements: Ace Bailey (62%) is the add if he's out there. He's put together two strong nights in a row, scoring at least 17 points with 10 boards and 3 assists and a block. Last year's No. 5 pick is getting a chance to showcase his talent. Jusuf Nurkić (foot) is also on the shelf, but when he's ready, he'll likely assume the starting center spot. For the deepest of leagues, Mo Bamba (10%) had 14 points, seven boards and four blocks in his first game of the season. His appeal fades if Jaxson Hayes (shoulder, 19%) and Markkanen return Wednesday. Indiana Pacers: Ivica Zubac Zubac rolled his left ankle Sunday against Brooklyn and is out Wednesday against Philadelphia. He's day-to-day as well, but no timetable has been provided for his return to play. The replacements: In the meantime, Jay Huff (18%) will likely start in place of Zu as he did on Monday. Expect some inconsistency, as seen by his 14 points with 3 assists and 3 blocks on Sunday, then posting a mere 6 points with 6 boards and no steals on Monday. He did play at least 20 minutes in each of those games. He's not a must-add for me, but someone else to watch is Obi Toppin (30%). Toppin ranks 61st in 9-cat through Tuesday and averages 15.8 points, 5 rebounds and 2.5 3s per game. Hurt before the season, still waiting to play Washington Wizards: AJ Dybantsa (ankle): The rookie No. 1 pick (90% rostered) will reportedly make his debut Wednesday against Cleveland. Charlotte Hornets: Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Coby White (calf): Neither has a timeline. Knueppel is 94% rostered and White is 83% and tumbling. Dennis Schröder and Grayson Allen benefit until their stars return to the lineup. San Antonio Spurs: Tobias Harris (calf): Harris missed valuable preseason time and hasn't suited up in a game this season. Fantasy managers should keep leaning on Julian Champagnie (32%), a strong source of points, 3s and, most recently, blocks. Chicago Bulls: Nic Claxton (hamstring): He's doing individual drills and hopes to practice next week. Jalen Smith (47%) is averaging 12.5 points and 7.5 boards as the starter. No matter how well Smith plays, the Bulls traded for Clax, and if healthy, he'll get the starting spot. Phoenix Suns: Mark Williams (shoulder): The report lists a February return. Khaman Maluach (56%) has started three games and is averaging 7.7 points and 7.3 rebounds. Not great, but if you need a big man in shallow leagues like High Score, Maluach is an option.

stories.title: Mavericks Injury Update: Santi Aldama could join the active roster this week
stories.summary: Aldama practiced with the Texas Legends on Tuesday and could return to the Mavericks’ active roster on Friday or Monday.
stories.detailText: DALLAS, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 25: Santi Aldama #34 of the Dallas Mavericks poses for portraits at Mavericks Media Day at American Airlines Center on September 25, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the GettyImages License Agreement. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Don’t let this little nugget go unnoticed. With so much going on in Mavsland, including an intriguing matchup on Wednesday against the Oklahoma City Thunder , some good news on the injury front may add another wrinkle to the vibes surrounding the team. The team’s PR machine announced on Tuesday that stretch big man Santi Aldama, whom the Mavericks acquired in a six-team draft day deal in July, has been assigned to the Texas Legends “to practice with the team as part of his return-to-play protocol.” Thrown in with that announcement is an upgrade for Aldama on the team’s injury report ahead of Wednesday’s game against the Thunder from “out” to “doubtful.” And on top of that, was this note attached to the end of the MavsPR update: “He will scrimmage with the team and be recalled following practice without appearing in any games for the Legends.” The Dallas Mavericks announced today that F Santi Aldama has been assigned to the Texas Legends to practice with the team as part of his return to play protocol. He will scrimmage with the team and be recalled following practice without appearing in any games for the Legends. — Mavs PR (@MavsPR) October 27, 2026 As of this writing, that scrimmage has likely already taken place. So, it should stand to reason, then, when the Dallas Morning News reported alongside the announcement that “it appears possible that Aldama could make his debut on either Friday or Monday.” Indeed, the PR machine basically confirmed as much when they gave a further update later in the day on Tuesday: that Aldama had been recalled from the Legends after practicing with the team. The Dallas Mavericks have recalled F Santi Aldama from the Texas Legends after he practiced with the club as part of his return to play protocol. — Mavs PR (@MavsPR) October 28, 2026 The Mavericks host the Houston Rockets on Friday and the Sacramento Kings on Monday in the last two legs of the team’s first homestand of the season. That Rockets game is also the first group-stage matchup of the NBA Cup for the Mavs. Dallas has turned some heads in the first four games of the season, with wins at the Indiana Pacers , in Tyrese Haliburton’s Welcome Home Game after missing last season recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon, and at the new-look Miami Heat , who remade their roster behind Giannis Antetokounmpo after nabbing the superstar in an offseason trade. Adding a stretch big to the mix after those early results, who scored 15 points per game last season (albeit in just 43 games), could elevate the Mavericks to a level many didn’t expect this year. Joining the team five or six games into the season is pretty close to the best-case scenario we wrote about in Aldama’s purposefully vague player preview profile before the season started. He’ll need time to work his way into shape and into his role in a new team at the same time. But if he can run the floor and fill lanes to shoot like he did with the Memphis Grizzlies, he definitely fits next to Cooper Flagg, as well as a true weapon off the bench. Santi Aldama is a unusual transition weapon for a 7-footer… One of the highest volume transition 7+ footers in the league. Runs the court well. Fills lanes to shoot. Gets to the rack. Can be weaponized running the floor next to Flagg. pic.twitter.com/dky0lhGxsh — Basketball University (@UofBasketball) September 16, 2026 He’s a versatile player. That gives us some level of confidence the veteran entering his sixth year will find a role and fill it successfully. A little bit of excitement is gathering behind this young Mavericks bunch. The news about Aldama’s injury status should only serve to fill the fanbase’s sails with a little more hot air.

teamStories.summary: A welcome return to the routine
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX -OCTOBER 27: The San Antonio Spurs starters and bench reacts after a dunk by Harrison Barnes #40 (not in photo) against Sacramento Kings in the second half at Frost Bank Center on October 27, 2026 in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images) | Getty Images None of this feels real to me. Not yet, anyway. It’s like we’re floating through an ethereal state of existence somewhere between awake and asleep. I can’t quite put my finger on it, but something still feels off. The season has started. The music is playing. The lights are on. Is anyone home? This was a win. From a basketball standpoint, the Spurs went out there against an overmatched Kings lineup and, mercifully, followed the script. They jumped on them immediately and never let up. Lobs, threes, blocks, the works. It all ran like a well-oiled machine, and we were treated to a comfortable, easy win that doesn’t require much analysis. The Spurs are better than the Kings. Let’s pack it up and call it a day, yeah? Because no one needs me to come into this space and tell you that when Julian Champagnie hits eight threes off the bench, the Spurs are hard to beat. It’s not breaking news that Wemby will have a big night if he gets unfettered access to the lane on barely contested pick-and-rolls. I’m not getting a Pulitzer for informing the noble readers of this site that if every team were the Sacramento Kings, we could start planning the parade right now. All due respect to the Kings, who I know are a real NBA team, but all of this brings me back to a nagging feeling in my gut that we’re stuck in some sort of basketball purgatory where nothing is beautiful and everything is fine. The stakes are real, but the outcomes feel perfunctory. Or maybe it’s just me. Look, I think I maybe died in June. Not literally, obviously, I’m still here typing away, but somewhere between the double-overtime Game 1 against OKC, the OG Tip-In, and the Knicks holding the trophy on our court, the part of me that does the feeling sort of got used up. I think I just forgot how much effort the playoffs require. How locked in you get, night after night after night. You redline it like that for long enough without the payoff of actually winning and then you’re just sitting there feeling empty. Waiting for it all to click on again. I wrote after the opening night Thunder game that I didn’t feel ready for the season to start, and I’m starting to think the season wasn’t ready either. The whole league seems to be out of whack in oddly specific ways. The Knicks hung their long-awaited banner and then became the first defending champs to start 0-3 since the 2011-12 Mavericks. The Nuggets got booed at their home opener, lost by 20 to the Warriors, and Jokic is snapping back at the crowd. The Heat got Giannis and promptly turned into the Bucks. I’m even seeing reports that LeBron James is a Sixer? That can’t be right. What else, what else. The Thunder are 4-0 and also might be in crisis. Jalen Williams was carried off the floor Sunday with a gruesome leg injury, Cason Wallace is headed for shoulder surgery, and Chet Holmgren is out with a bad knee. Are they, like, already maybe done? The new-look Wolves were off to a great start until word came down Tuesday that Ant is having knee surgery and will miss up to two months, a day after he scored 47 playing on it. Even Certified Iron Man Kawhi Leonard might miss some time with a swollen knee! (Ok, actually that checks out.) Meanwhile, Memphis and Portland are sitting near the top of the West. Just like we all predicted! In that sense, I suppose the relatively routine nature of the Spurs romping over the Kings last night was a welcome sign of life. Something happened the way it was supposed to. The shots went in. No one got hurt. The crowd cheered and we all moved on to the next thing. I just can’t wrap my arms around any of it yet, and I don’t think I want to. This is the preseason, for all intents and purposes. From now on, I’m going to try to just let this stuff happen however it needs to happen. Go smooth-brained with it. Shake off the losses, ignore the wins, and clap like a seal when there’s a big dunk or a loud noise. It’s fine. It’s all fine. Or it’s not. Whatever. Late in the fourth quarter, with the game long decided, Harrison Barnes rose up over Alex Karaban and the whole building went nuts as he threw it down. The bench was on its feet. The announcers fell apart. Wemby even said afterward that he stood up so quick he got dizzy, and his explanation for all the commotion was simply that everybody loves Barnes. Maybe that’s it. The season started before we were ready and we simply stood up too fast. The blood rushed to our heads, the room tilted a bit, and the whole place got a little too loud for a few seconds. We couldn’t tell whether we were waking up or just finally losing it for good. Honestly, I’ll take either. In a league where up is down and left is right, the most meaningful thing that happened in this game was a dunk that didn’t matter. It could be that it was just nice to feel some synapses firing again, if only for a moment. We’re all losing our minds. Or maybe we lost them already. Either way, the lights are on. It’s time to go home. Takeaways: I just can’t help feeling like the season doesn’t actually start until Tobias Harris gets in the mix. He’s the skeleton key that unlocks this whole thing. Has to be. It’s really frustrating to watch this game and feel like this is how the whole thing is supposed to look but, because it came against the Kings, it’s hard to feel like it matters. It’s a scientific result that happened in a vacuum. It’s a scrimmage against cardboard cutouts and traffic cones. I liked it. I was happy with it. I don’t trust it even a little bit. That said, made shots beget made shots beget made shots. Mitch has emphasized a few times this season that the process for getting looks has been good and that the shots going in was a matter of time. Well, tonight they went in. The Spurs came in shooting 31.2 percent from three and went 17-of-37, including 13-of-22 before halftime, and we were all treated to just how effective this offense can look when that happens. I know Wemby can’t be this aggressive against every team, but it would have been more worrying if he hadn’t taken full advantage of a night like this. He missed all three of his threes and still scored 29, because 18 of his 21 shots were twos, including nine dunks, five of them off lobs. So everyone here at WWL headquarters is going to go ahead and give him a polite golf clap anyway. WWL Post Game Press Conference So you’re having trouble getting out of the blocks this season? I really am. I wish I could say that I’ll stop talking about it sometime soon but I’m not sure I can make that kind of a commitment. I’m adrift. I’m waltzing around in no man’s land. I’m lost on the Penrose stairs in an infinite loop of wondering when this season will feel like it’s actually real. It seems to me like you flew too close to the sun and now you’re trying to dig out of the hole with as many metaphors as possible. I’m looking for any port in a storm. Sounds like you’re just spinning your wheels. I’m certainly burning the candle at both ends, I’ll tell you that much for free. Maybe you’re missing the forest for the trees? I probably just put the cart before the horse. It’s still early, no need to clutch at straws just yet. I’ll try not to beat a dead horse. Remember, it’s a marathon, not a sprint. Gotta keep pounding the rock.

teamStories.title: NBA Power Rankings: How all 30 teams stack up after one week
teamStories.summary: Here's where all 30 NBA teams rank after one week of the 2026-27 regular season, plus the most surprising statistic or trend for each franchise.
teamStories.detailText: It has been a little over a week since the start of the 2026-27 NBA regular season, and we've already had a jam-packed couple of days filled with surprise starts, star returns and a few disappointing debuts. LeBron James kicked off his 24th season with the new-look Philadelphia 76ers by defeating the defending champs -- the New York Knicks -- after their ring ceremony at Madison Square Garden and displaying early positive returns following a busy offseason. On the flip side, the San Antonio Spurs , after a Finals appearance in June, are struggling behind young superstar Victor Wembanyama . However, their cross-state rivals, the Houston Rockets , are one of four undefeated teams left in the Western Conference, along with the Oklahoma City Thunder (the 2024-25 champions), the Memphis Grizzlies and the Portland Trail Blazers . In our first iteration of Power Rankings since the campaign started, our NBA insiders break down their biggest observations from opening week, including the most surprising statistic or trend for every team, and what to expect as teams try to find their footing or build on their momentum. Note: Team rankings are based on where members of our panel (ESPN's Jamal Collier, Michael C. Wright, Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Ben Golliver, Kris Rhim and Anthony Slater) think teams belong. Previous rankings: Preseason Jump to a team: ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS 1. Oklahoma City Thunder 2026-27 record: 4-0 Previous ranking: 1 Next games: @ DAL (Oct. 28), @ HOU (Oct. 31), @ CLE (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Third-year guard Ajay Mitchell 's elevated role. In the wake of the serious injuries suffered by Jalen Williams (fibula/ankle) and Cason Wallace (shoulder), Mitchell should see an increased role on the floor. He has repeatedly shown that he can thrive as the No. 2 offensive option alongside two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander . Mitchell averaged 22.5 points and 6.0 assists in the Thunder's sweep of the Lakers in last season's Western Conference semifinals, when Williams was sidelined. Mitchell had a career-high 30 points and five assists in Monday's win over the Suns, his first start of the season. -- Tim MacMahon 2. Minnesota Timberwolves 2026-27 record: 3-1 Previous ranking: 5 Next games: vs. GS (Oct. 28), vs. LAC (Oct. 30), @ SA (Oct. 31), vs. MIL (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 120.8 offensive rating. Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball 's instant chemistry was marvelous : Minnesota's new-look starting lineup outscored opponents by 31 points in 56 minutes through four games. Meanwhile, the Timberwolves posted a 120.8 offensive rating when their dynamic guard duo shared the court -- an exceptional mark that would have ranked second in the NBA last season. However, that could all come to a halt as Edwards will be sidelined up to two months , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday, after he undergoes an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee. -- Ben Golliver 3. Detroit Pistons 2026-27 record: 3-1 Previous ranking: 7 Next games: vs. CHA (Oct. 28), @ BKN (Oct. 30), @ CHA (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 42%. That's what the previously anemic Pistons have shot from 3 in the first three games this season. Duncan Robinson leads the league in makes per game (5.0) and is shooting a blistering 54% from distance, while newcomer John Collins is taking nearly five a night at a 50% clip. Last season, this team was barely near the league average and struggled at creating and making shots in the playoffs, leading to their second-round loss to Cleveland. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Robinson is more comfortable looking for shots and taking contested ones, which also means some regression to the mean will occur. But being more aggressive is a positive sign of sorts. -- Vincent Goodwill 4. Houston Rockets 2026-27 record: 4-0 Previous ranking: 10 Next games: @ MIL (Oct. 28), @ DAL (Oct. 30), vs. OKC (Oct. 31), vs. BOS (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 4-0 start . For the first time since 2014-15, Houston is off to a 4-0 start and finally playing the way it was expected to last season when it first acquired Kevin Durant . The return of veteran point guard Fred VanVleet , who missed last season with a torn ACL, has played a role in Durant starting off the season with four straight 20-point games for the 10th time in his career. Meanwhile, big man Alperen Sengun is feasting off the order VanVleet has restored to the offense, becoming just the third Rocket to put together multiple 25-5-5 games within the first four games of the season. -- Michael C. Wright 5. Philadelphia 76ers 2026-27 record: 3-1 Previous ranking: 4 Next games: @ IND (Oct. 28), vs. NYK (Oct. 30), @ CHA (Oct. 31), vs. CHI (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 8.8. The Sixers averaged 8.8 offensive rebounds per game. As the Sixers struggled to rebound in the preseason, coach Nick Nurse wasn't concerned. "We're going to be a good rebounding team," he said then. The Sixers still aren't, ranking 29th in the NBA in offensive rebounding per game and 26th in total rebounds per game. The struggles make some sense as the Sixers' front court has been decimated with injury, but it remains concerning and something Nurse is hoping they fix quickly. "I think that our guys understand that we got to do a better job," he said. -- Kris Rhim 6. Los Angeles Lakers 2026-27 record: 3-1 Previous ranking: 11 Next games: @ LAC (Oct. 28), @ GS (Oct. 30), vs. TOR (Nov. 1), vs. MIA (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 60/60/90. Austin Reaves got off to an unbelievably hot start through the Lakers' 3-0 showing out of the gates, averaging a career-best 26.7 points on 63.9% from the field, 61.5% from 3 and 89.7% from the free throw line entering Tuesday's game. He and Luka Doncic (34.3 points per game) are the only pair of teammates in the top 10 in scoring in the league. They would be even more effective if they took care of the ball better. They also both rank in the top 10 in turnovers per game through three games, with 7.0 for Doncic and 4.3 for Reaves. -- Dave McMenamin 7. Toronto Raptors 2026-27 record: 2-1 Previous ranking: 12 Next games: vs. ORL (Oct. 28), vs. ORL (Oct. 30), @ LAL (Nov. 1), @ LAC (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 0-12. The Raptors' only loss this season came with Kawhi Leonard sidelined, but Toronto will be without Leonard for a period of weeks as he manages left knee soreness. The concerning part about life without Leonard is that in the Raptors' first look without him, Scottie Barnes had one of the worst outings of his career, finishing 0-12 with three turnovers and a team-worst minus-27 in the 117-94 loss. -- Rhim 8. Boston Celtics 2026-27 record: 3-1 Previous ranking: 6 Next games: vs. CHI (Oct. 30), @ ORL (Nov. 1), @ HOU (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Jordan Walsh is in the starting lineup. Starting Walsh, a rotational player who started 25 games last season, came as a bit of a surprise with veterans such as Sam Hauser and Payton Pritchard on the roster. But so far, Walsh's defense has buoyed the Celtics early in the season, slowing down guards including the Knicks' Jalen Brunson (2-for-7, five points against Walsh) and the Pistons' Cade Cunningham (1-for-3, three points against Walsh), according to NBA.com. -- Rhim 9. San Antonio Spurs 2026-27 record: 2-2 Previous ranking: 2 Next games: @ UTAH (Oct. 28), vs. MIN (Oct. 31), vs. UTAH (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 0 -2 start. The Spurs ran into the combustible mixture of growing pains in trying to evolve their offense with a new starting five while facing two of the West's toughest teams -- Oklahoma City and Houston -- to start the season. So, the early struggles weren't unexpected, and the Spurs are comfortable with taking their lumps early. But in the process of trying to raise its ceiling, San Antonio lowered its floor, a disturbing early trend. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said, "We've got to just keep getting back to the standard we know we are capable of. Our floor right now is way too low." -- Wright 10. Portland Trail Blazers 2026-27 record: 3-0 Previous ranking: 17 Next games: vs. MEM (Oct. 29), @ UTAH (Oct. 31), @ DEN (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 21-0 lead. The Blazers enjoyed the perfect start to the intriguing Damian Lillard and Ja Morant partnership thanks to a blowout win over the Suns in their season opener. Portland raced out to a 21-0 lead in front of a raucous Moda Center crowd that eagerly welcomed Lillard back from an Achilles injury. Though Morant opened the season as a starter, he has had to make great sacrifices to fit into Portland's crowded backcourt rotation. The two-time All-Star is tracking toward career lows in minutes, points, shots and usage rate. -- Golliver 11. Indiana Pacers 2026-27 record: 2-2 Previous ranking: 13 Next games: vs. PHI (Oct. 28), @ MIA (Oct. 30), vs. BKN (Nov. 1), vs. ATL (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 21.8. The number of points Tyrese Haliburton is averaging through his first four games back from injury. He has scored at least 20 in three of the first four games of a season for only the second time in his career, played in a back-to-back this week and he's averaging 9.5 assists. Any worries about him needing to ease back into action have been unfounded. Haliburton looks like his old self after missing 16 months, but the Pacers are going to need to get healthier around him. ( Ivica Zubac has a sprained left ankle, T.J. McConnell has yet to play in a game in either preseason or regular season and Ben Sheppard tore his meniscus.) -- Jamal Collier 12. Denver Nuggets 2026-27 record: 1-2 Previous ranking: 8 Next games: @ NO (Oct. 28), @ PHX (Oct. 30), vs. POR (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: The Nuggets' 119.3 defensive rating is fifth worst in the league. It's been a strange first homestand for the Nuggets. They fell 23 points to the Pelicans and even received some boos, but then stormed back for an overtime win with help from rookie Trevon Brazile , who made a handful of spectacular plays and looks like a second-round steal at a time Denver desperately needs depth. After the game, Nikola Jokic called out the jeering fans, saying they weren't welcome back, and doubled down a couple of nights later after they were blown out at home by the previously winless Warriors. -- Anthony Slater 13. Cleveland Cavaliers 2026-27 record: 2-1 Previous ranking: 9 Next games: vs. WAS (Oct. 28), @ ATL (Oct. 29), @ MIL (Oct. 31), vs. OKC (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Keep an eye on the wing trio of Peyton Watson , Sam Merrill and Jaylon Tyson and how they complement Cleveland's core four throughout the season. That trio has made just 19.5% of their combined 3-pointers so far -- but it's still very early, so there's plenty of time for those role players to turn it around and start making more shots in support of the stars. -- Zach Kram 14. Memphis Grizzlies 2026-27 record: 4-0 Previous ranking: 24 Next games: @ POR (Oct. 29), vs. SAC (Oct. 31), vs. NO (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Ty Jerome 's hot start and the Grizzlies 4-0 start. Memphis' 4-0 start ranks as the second best in franchise history behind the 2014-15 campaign in which the Grizzlies won their first six games. Perhaps the most eye-popping early trend comes from the way this young team has performed in clutch time. Three of Memphis' first four outings turned out to be clutch-time games, with the Grizzlies winning all of them to tie the 76ers for the most clutch wins so far this season. Jerome ranks third in the league in scoring (29.8 points per game) after a career-high 45-point season opener, which he then followed with 31 points against the Kings. -- Wright 15. Atlanta Hawks 2026-27 record: 2-2 Previous ranking: 15 Next games: vs. MIA (Oct. 28), vs. CLE (Oct. 29), @ NO (Oct. 31), @ IND (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Can Quin Snyder continue to rely heavily on his rotation? One storyline entering the season was whether the Hawks' frontcourt could succeed against quality opponents. The loss at Houston proved they have a long way to go. In the 10-point loss, Atlanta was outrebounded 40-22 on the offensive glass (52-35 overall) and were minus-11 in free-throw attempts. The lone frontcourt player with a positive plus-minus was Onyeka Okongwu . Through the first four games, nine players have averaged more than 18 MPG, with only starter Jalen Johnson averaging more than 30 MPG. -- Bobby Marks 16. New York Knicks 2026-27 record: 1-3 Previous ranking: 3 Next games: @ CHI (Oct. 28), @ PHI (Oct. 30), vs. BKN (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 30th. That's where the Knicks ranked in both offensive efficiency and raw scoring entering Tuesday's game. It's a small sample size, but the Knicks have barely shown more than flashes of that potent offense. "We get a little comfortable," Jalen Brunson said after Sunday's loss to Orlando, in which New York gave up 40 fourth-quarter points to the Magic. Before Tuesday, Mikal Bridges registered donuts at the foul line and 3-point line. One is expected, the other is not. -- Goodwill 17. Charlotte Hornets 2026-27 record: 3-1 Previous ranking: 23 Next games: @ DET (Oct. 28), @ WAS (Oct. 30), vs. PHI (Oct. 31), vs. DET (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 36.3 PPG. New Hornets Grayson Allen and Naz Reid came to Charlotte in trades for Miles Bridges and LaMelo Ball, respectively, and both sharpshooters are excelling in their new digs. Allen and Reid have combined to average 36.3 points per game while making 44% of their 3-pointers, and both players rank in the top 10 in the NBA in made 3s. -- Kram 18. Washington Wizards 2026-27 record: 2-2 Previous ranking: 22 Next games: @ CLE (Oct. 28), vs. CHA (Oct. 30), @ ORL (Nov. 2 Most surprising stat or trend: 8.8 PPG. After averaging 16.3 points per game with a 26% usage rate in a promising sophomore season, Alex Sarr is down to 8.8 PPG with a 14% usage rate this year. That decline epitomizes the difficult balancing act for the Wizards as they try to win games with veteran stars Trae Young and Anthony Davis , while also providing opportunities for their many prospects to develop on the court. -- Kram 19. Phoenix Suns 2026-27 record: 1-2 Previous ranking: 18 Next games: vs. DEN (Oct. 30), @ GS (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 40. Devin Booker recorded the 40th 40-point game of his career with 43 points on 17-of-25 shooting in the Suns' 131-122 win over the Warriors opening week. It's the most in franchise history, with Amar'e Stoudemire trailing significantly behind at No. 2 with 15 of them. stories.title: Brian Thomas Jr. trying to ignore trade talk, 'keep working hard' for Jaguars
stories.summary: Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. said Wednesday he isn't concerned about being the subject of recent trade rumors.
stories.detailText: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr . said Wednesday he isn't concerned about being the subject of recent trade rumors. And he isn't wasting time worrying about his future with the team, either. After all, he's been there before. "Everybody's entitled to their own opinion," Thomas, a Pro Bowler as a rookie, said. "I just go out there, do what I do, and just try to go out there and be the best player I can be." For some, that opinion is that Thomas needs a change of scenery and that the Jaguars would be better off trading the third-year receiver, especially after his disappointing performance against the Houston Texans in London on Oct. 18. Thomas dropped one pass and failed to come up with a catchable throw in the first half of that game, then didn't play a snap in the second half of the 34-31 loss, later leaving the Wembley Stadium locker room without talking to reporters. On the season, Thomas now has four drops, per ESPN Research. Thomas on Wednesday said he wanted to "flush" that game and move forward with a different mindset. "Everybody goes through adversity," he said. "You've just got to keep fighting through it. That's the only way I know how to get through, just keep fighting through it. And that's what I'm going to continue to do, keep fighting and keep coming in with a good mindset, keep working hard each and every day at practice. "Going out there, doing the little things, trying to be the best that I can be, blocking, doing all the little things, just keep fighting through it." Thomas has just nine catches for 105 yards and a touchdown in six games this season, yet coach Liam Coen said Wednesday he remains a significant part of the offense. "Every player has ups and downs," Coen said. "I fully anticipate he's going to make plays for us this Sunday (against the Colts )." Thomas has been the subject of trade rumors in the past. Before the start of free agency this spring, Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said the team was not trying to trade Thomas and called any reports that it was shopping him "fraudulent claims." Thomas set a franchise rookie record with 1,282 yards receiving -- which ranked third in the NFL -- and had 10 TD catches in 2024 , when he made the Pro Bowl. Expectations for him in 2025 were high, especially after Coen said at the NFL scouting combine that year he planned to run the pass offense through the former LSU star. But Thomas looked uncomfortable during training camp that season. In addition to learning the new offense, he and quarterback Trevor Lawrence had some issues connecting on throws. It continued into the regular season, when Thomas dropped five passes in the first five games -- including a fourth-down drop inside the 10-yard line in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals . There were also several instances when he appeared to shy away from contact. Thomas finished his second season with 48 catches for 707 yards and two touchdowns in 14 games. This year, expectations for Thomas rose again after he had a strong training camp. But two drops in a Week 2 loss to the Denver Broncos and the two against the Texans cranked up the trade speculation. Thomas is trying his best to ignore it -- again. "I try not to be too up, too down, too low," Thomas said. "So I try to stay [in the middle]. So just trying to tune all that out and just stay focused, stay locked in on the main thing."

stories.title: Jets WR Garrett Wilson says he doesn't want to be traded but does want to win
stories.summary: Jets receiver Garrett Wilson says he doesn't want to be traded but he expressed that he's frustrated by his target share and, most of all, losing.
stories.detailText: FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson made two things abundantly clear Wednesday: He doesn't want to be traded, but he's extremely frustrated by his lack of involvement in the offense and, most of all, the losing. "Yeah, I want to be here, man," Wilson said. "I want to win games and that's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful. "I've never been the best optimistic guy, but I've found a way and dug deep, and I've been optimistic for three, four, five years now. And that's why these [losses] each weekend hurt a little more." Wilson was visibly upset on the sideline in the fourth quarter of the Jets' 28-25 loss to the previously winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday. He was targeted only three times in the game (two catches for 26 yards), one week after he was a non-factor in a loss to the New England Patriots . His frustration, coupled with the Nov. 10 trade deadline, has fueled speculation about his desire to remain in New York. Fifteen months ago, he signed a four-year, $130 million contract extension through 2030. The Jets dealt cornerback Sauce Gardner at the deadline last year a few months after he signed a four-year, $120 million extension. In this case, there is no indication they're looking to trade Wilson, 26, who leads the team with 37 receptions and 444 yards. Likewise, Wilson said he wants to stay, but his desire to be in a winning situation could prompt a change of heart in the offseason. He said the losing, coupled with limited opportunities, exacerbates his frustration. "No doubt, no doubt," he said. "I'd be lying if I said it's not, but at the end of the day it comes down to ... winning and losing. Throughout my experience, when things go right, I tend to have a part in that. And when it doesn't, it seems avoidable. "That's my main frustration that may show on the TV or something like that. But I don't want it to ever be misconstrued. This all comes from a place in my heart of wanting to win. I'm biased, but it also comes from experience where I played my part in that. "It's frustrating, for sure, because I want to have an impact and I want to help the team. But, really, I just want to help the team, man. Sometimes it might come off a certain way when they [show] video, but, man, that's all it's about." Wilson was the No. 10 pick in 2022. Since then, the Jets are 24-41, including 2-5 this season. They host the Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) on Sunday. Coach Aaron Glenn has said repeatedly they want to get the ball to Wilson early and often. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich and quarterback Geno Smith have echoed those sentiments. "I've always said this: I'm looking to get him the football as much as I can, but I have to be mindful of what the defense is doing as well," Smith said. The coaches have said Wilson is drawing extra coverage, creating opportunities for others in the passing game. Wilson took issue with that perception, saying, "I wouldn't say anyone's doing anything Houdini or a superpower to try and take me away." Wilson said he enjoys seeing his fellow receivers thrive, but he added, "Attracting more coverage? I don't know. I always want to make people earn their flowers is how I see it. ... So, they have to cover it. They've got to cover me. If they can't prove they could do it, I don't believe they could do it. And that's just how I operate, how my mindset is." He said he hasn't shared his opinion with his coaches, saying, "I think it's understood." One player who would welcome a change of scenery is cornerback Nahshon Wright , who told ESPN he's "definitely frustrated" by his lack of playing time. Wright, who made five interceptions last season for the Chicago Bears , has yet to play a snap on defense. Asked if he has requested a trade, Wright said, "Not formally." He added, "I've expressed my feelings [to the team]. I think I've earned that right." He signed a one-year, $3.5 million contract (fully guaranteed), thinking he'd compete for a starting job. He missed time in training camp due to an injury and lost out to Azareye'h Thomas . "I'm open to anything at this point," Wright said. "I just want to go where I can play, whether it's here or somewhere else. I just want to contribute. I know what I can do and I think I put that on display [last season]. So, yeah, it's definitely frustrating."

stories.title: Kansas State Football: Depth Chart Review – Arizona State
stories.summary: The Kansas State defense kept the team in the game but faded in the 4th quarter.
stories.detailText: TEMPE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 24: Cardae Mack #25 of the Arizona State Sun Devils rushes the football against the Kansas State Wildcats during the game at Sun Devil Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Tempe, Arizona. The Sun Devils defeated the Wildcats 28-17. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Defensive Line Note: Starters are bolded, stats from Pro Football Focus and ESPN Defensive End Wendell Gregory: Snaps – 46 – Tackles – 4 – Sacks – 1 – T.F.L. – 1 Jordan Allen: Snaps – 40 – Tackles – 8 – Sacks – 2 – T.F.L. – 2 Darien Whitaker Jr.: Snaps – 42 – Tackles – 1 Jayden Bryant: Snaps – 29 – Tackles – 1 – Sacks – 1 – T.F.L. – 1 Nose Tackle Kamari Burns: Snaps – 25 – Tackles – 2 Defensive Tackle Travis Bates: Snaps – 63 – No Stats Eli Jackson: Snaps – 33 – Tackles – 1 De’Arieun Hicks: Snaps – 6 – Tackles – 1 Grade: C+ This unit is tough to grade. Arizona State’s lead back, Cardae Mack, rushed for 159 yards and 4 touchdowns on 26 attempts. Normally, that falls on the defensive line, and while they share some of the blame, a good bit also falls on the linebacker and safeties. Even though the run defense struggled, the pass rush was consistent. Once again, the defensive ends lived in the backfield, generating 10 quarterback pressures, including 4 sacks and 3 hits on the Sun Devil’s quarterback. One of those quarterback hits knocked ASU starter Mikey Keene out of the game with a leg injury, which, in retrospect, may have hurt Kansas State more than it helped. Jordan Allen, on the other hand, played his best game of the season by far. He looks as close to 100% as you can be at this point in the season, and he’s shaken off the rust from missing time early in the year. He was the best player on the field for the Wildcats, on either side of the ball. He led the team with 2 sacks and also batted down a pass at the line of scrimmage. He also recorded 2 run stops, but he missed a tackle. If Kansas State can get this type of performance from Allen on a regular basis, they’ll continue to have one of the more disruptive defensive lines in the nation. Speaking of disruptive, Wendell Gregory continues to terrorize Big 12 quarterbacks. He was credited with a team-high 3 quarterback pressures, including a sack. Unfortunately, his pass-rush acumen didn’t translate to the run game. To his credit, he made a tackle for loss, but he also missed 2 tackles. Arizona State made it a point to run at the Wildcat’s athletic defensive ends, and found solid success. Former starter Darrien Whitaker Jr. has transitioned to a more pass-rush-centric role with Allen back in the fold. That’s good, because he’s a bit of a one-trick pony. He managed 2 hits on the quarterback in 19 pass-rush attempts but recorded only 1 missed tackle on 19 rush attempts. He has the potential to be a star but needs to toughen up his run defense and stop relying solely on his athletic ability. If he doesn’t, teams will run at him whenever he’s on the field. Last but not least, all Jayden Bryant does is produce when he’s on the field. He recorded another sack against Arizona State and earned an additional hurry in 18 pass-rush opportunities. Like Whitaker Jr., he’s mostly used on clear passing downs. On the interior line, Travis Bates returned to his cardio-centric play after turning in his best performance of the season against Kansas. The defensive staff bets that Bates’s productivity will offset the fact that he’s a defensive end playing defensive tackle. He was credited with a hit on the quarterback but recorded no stats on 30 Arizona State rushing attempts. Kansas State lost their bet last week. Eli Jackson and Kamari Burns continue to split time at the other defensive tackle spot. Together, they recorded 4 stops in the run game, which wouldn’t be terrible if Bates were more productive. That wasn’t the case on Saturday. Arizona State did most of their damage in the run game on the edges, so that’s a positive note for the defensive tackles at least. Linebacker Middle Linebacker Gabe Powers: Snaps – 18 – Tackles – 4 Asa Newsom: Snaps – 25 – Tackles – 4 – T.F.L. – 1 Weak Side Linebacker Mekhi Mason: Snaps – 64 – Tackles – 7 – T.F.L. – 1 Rex Van Wyhe: Snaps – 41 – Tackles – 5 Grade: C Gabe Powers gave it the ole’ college try but only lasted 18 snaps after suffering an injury last week. That left most linebacker snaps to Mekhi Mason and Rex Van Wyhe. I’m a Van Wyhe fan, but I like him in smaller, more concentrated doses. He’s not a sideline-to-sideline linebacker like Powers, and Arizona State focused on attacking the edges for the Kansas State defense. Mason played well, but his role shifts when Powers is off the field. With Powers, he can stay inside and utilize his running-stuffing ability. With Van Wyhe, he ends up playing more on the edges, where he’s still good, but has to rely more on his speed, which isn’t his strongest suit. Defensive Coordinator Jordan Peterson’s answer to the speed problem at linebacker was to give Asa Newsom the most action he’s seen this season. Like Jordan Allen, Asa was banged up in camp and couldn’t give the new defensive staff a true accounting of his talent. In terms of playing style, his game is closer to Powers than Van Wyhe; that helps Mason as well. I think you’ll see more Newsom and less Van Wyhe moving forward if Powers remains limited. This group was OK, but their lack of speed was exploited on perimeter runs. Secondary Cornerback JoJo Scott: Snaps – 57- Tackles – 4 – Targeted – 9 – Rec Al . – 4 – Yds – 91 Zashon Rich: Snaps – 55 – Tackles – 5 – Targeted – 9 – Rec Al. – 5 – Yds – 88 Kaleb Patterson: Snaps – 44 – No Stats – Targeted – 2 – Rec. They went after Scott early and often, and while he was credited with 2 pass breakups and 2 forced incompletions, he also gave up a 51-yard reception and committed a pass interference penalty. He started on the outside but gave way to Kaleb Patterson and moved back to his more familiar slot corner position. JoJo has been a revelation for the Wildcat secondary this season, but life is a little different under the microscope on the outside. Nick McClellan started the game at slot corner and did a solid job. He was targeted once and gave up 1 reception, but it only covered 6 yards. He’ll continue to get bench snaps this season, but he should be in a prime position to start at slot corner next season (all portal disclaimers apply). Speaking of which, Zashon Rich returned to the starting lineup after starting the game on the bench against Kansas, following his lackluster performance against Houston. He responded with a solid game, including pass breakups and 3 forced interceptions. Unfortunately, he also gave up 17.6 yards per reception, including a 39-yard pass. Like Rich, Kaleb Patterson found himself on the bench against Kansas because of the Houston game. Unlike Rich, he didn’t leave the bench against the Jayhawks. He was back in the mix against ASU and held up well, giving up only 6 yards; meanwhile, JoJo Scott dealt with the traffic he usually faced as CB2 on the outside. I wouldn’t be surprised if Patterson returned to the starting corner spot in the next game. Free Safety Koy Beasley: Snaps – 71 – Tackles – 6 – Targeted – 2 – Rec Al. – 1 – Yds – 22 Strong Safety Logan Bartley : Snaps – 72 – Tackles – 11 – Targeted – 6 – Rec Al. – 4 – Yds – 46 Safety Grade: C Bartley led the team with 11 tackles, including 5 run stops, and didn’t miss a tackle. Jordan Allen was the best player on defense, but Bartley was close behind. At this point, he’s more of a de facto linebacker than a strong safety. He lined up in the run box 53 and did a good job of getting outside and keeping ASU from doing even more damage with their outside run game. He’s another player who projects as a key part of the Kansas State defense moving forward (transfer portal disclaimer). Unfortunately, this wasn’t a great game for Koy Beasley. Keep in mind, he’s listed at 5’10”, 185 pounds, and that’s on a tall day after a breakfast buffet. He was active in run defense, making 5 tackles, but he also missed 3. I still don’t understand why Jordan Peterson refuses to use more than one player at this position. Beasley is a slot corner playing free safety. He’s the fastest player on the team and can handle being the only deep safety because he covers so much ground. The problem occurs when Beasley has to line up as a box safety and make tackles in the run game. I remember one of his “missed” tackles where he tried to put a shoulder into a running back and bounced off like the back was utilizing a force field. Continuity in the back end helps reduce mistakes, and Beasley’s speed lets Peterson unleash Bartley, but I’d rather have one of the other safeties on the field when the opposition runs outside in the alleys. I’m not sure what Wesley Fair has done to get buried on the depth chart, because I’d take him over Beasley 10/10 times when it comes to making a play in the run game. I’d take Beasley over Fair 10/10 times in coverage. Combined, they make a balanced safety, but Beasley on his own leaves much to be desired.

stories.title: Are Buffalo Bills fans’ expectations out of sync with 5-1 record?
stories.summary: How are you feeling about the 5-1 Buffalo Bills after their bye week, and ahead of Week 8 vs. Baltimore Ravens?
stories.detailText: LAS VEGAS, NV - OCTOBER 18: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills warms up before kickoff against the Las Vegas Raiders during an NFL football game at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The bye week was fruitful for the Buffalo Bills. Losses by three key AFC foes in the New England Patriots, Baltimore Ravens, and Kansas City Chiefs now set Buffalo up with a real opportunity to earn the one seed at season’s end. They just have to keep winning. The last time we saw the Bills in action, they pulled off a 33-30 road win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Saying “pulled off” against the .500 Raiders team may seem uncomfortable, but that’s what transpired in their 33-30 victory in Week 6. A game that many felt Buffalo should have had well in hand came down to the wire, thanks in part to a mostly ineffective defense that once again struggled to stop an opponent’s passing attack. It’s become a broken record, this continued discussion about what ails the Bills’ defense. In truth, it’s almost everything related to playing defense. Even the once-potent pass rush has cooled to a mild simmer more reminiscent of airport wings than your favorite Buffalo hang. Much of that is due to the way teams are playing the defense. Okay, yes, all is not doom and gloom for a 5-1 team that currently shares the lead in the AFC. It’s a long season and with that comes the potential for Buffalo’s defense to put it all together and make something big out of their first year under defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. Until and unless that happens, success is likely to hinge on the offense being able to score on nearly every drive. Take a step back for a minute though, and ask yourself if you thought the Bills would be 5-1 under rookie head coach Joe Brady? Maybe it’s an easy “yes” simply due to quarterback Josh Allen. Before deciding if that’s the case, consider the rash of injuries on offense, and some turnover-heavy performances. Then take a minute and reflect on the type of player Greg Rousseau has become, and what’s becoming true of defensive tackle Deone Walker. There are encouraging signs and plenty of tape to prove this team has enough to hang with the big boys. Remember, Josh Allen is one of the game’s most incredible players. So many fans believe that One Bills Drive should be doing more to pull off an impactful trade. Too much of that discourse fails to realize Buffalo’s current cap situations, which affords them around $4 million in available money. Even if they could finalize a trade for your favorite player, how are they fitting any impactful starter’s current salary on the books? With that said, how are you feeling about the team? After some time to think things over through the bye week, are you confident in the Bills currently under the direction of Joe Brady and president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane?
